account:
Today I am keeping my usual appointments: morning office business, the ten o'clock mill grain inspection, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, and Builder's office review at sixteen thirty. At the mill I inspected the stall chest and found two stacks of 64 hay bales, advertised at two emeralds apiece. That confirms stock is present, but nobody has yet answered my questions about storage conditions or delivery reliability.

The unusual thing is repeated, vague news about a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Several townsfolk repeat almost the same words. They place Baker there, sometimes with Neighbour, and report Baker carrying a sack of bread. I have not seen a change myself, and those reports do not explain whether it concerns a route, a delivery arrangement, or something else. A sack of bread alone is not suspicious for a baker. Neighbour earlier said Freight wanted to know when I would inspect the mill and would be at the east landing that morning. I have now asked Neighbour what the reported change actually means and whether Freight had a concern, but have not received an explanation.

Separately, Builder is conducting an authorized two-emerald inspection of town hall doors, bridge decking, and the east ferry landing, with written findings due at sixteen thirty. His preliminary report said no visible bridge defects and a normally working entrance door. No repairs are authorized. There was confusion over which landing and how to supply writing materials; I clarified the east landing and gave Secretary one emerald for an office writable book so she can transcribe his findings for his review. That inspection is intended to identify actual maintenance needs before committing repair funds. I have no evidence that it explains the bakery reports, so I should keep those matters separate until someone provides specifics.
